future_check: All five public rays terminate at a boundary; active-stopper termination is retained at 15.08-15.52% because it is explicit in the executable rule, but this unobserved output branch caps oracle and training ratings at tier 3.; The strict rate is 9.56-9.96%, close to the explicit 10% profile prior. Returned-grid classification includes incidental matches and ignores only independently proven off-route decoys.; Difficulty separation applies to ordinary routes: easy uses 8..12 with 0..1 decoys, medium 10..16 with 1..2, and hard 14..20 with 2..3. Public-profile injection deliberately keeps every demonstrated size/decoy form reachable in every band.; The clean grammar excludes zero/four-turn routes, corner/interior sources, loops, dense decoys, and paths shorter than three even though the total Racket oracle defines many of them. Those forms remain parity-tested rather than training-weighted.; Task-local Racket lint reports three style-eq-zero warnings and zero errors. Replacing `(= x 0)` with `zero?` would be cosmetic and would churn synchronized canonical/base authority, so the warnings are recorded rather than edited.; Published held-out output was visible during verification under repository policy. The generator embeds only public input scene profiles and never reads output tables.; Version 3 deliberately breaks replay compatibility with 2.0 because the old distribution omitted the core mirror operation in 79.9% of draws and never produced a complete linked profile; deterministic replay is guaranteed within 3.0.0.; Worker-side gates establish a candidate repair, not independent acceptance. The tier-3 recommendation remains provisional until monitor v13 passes this exact source/record digest and the regenerated queue says reviewed_safe.
rationale: VERSION 2.0.0 -> 3.0.0: replaced random object scattering with constructive simple routes whose one through three mirrors are actually encountered in order by the returned beam.; Added a calibrated 10% default-only prior over the complete answer-bearing D4 orbits of all five public scenes. Off-route mirror/stopper count, color, and position are resampled because they provably do not affect the traced output.; Separated active route objects from off-route decoys. Every ordinary lesson now contains one through three active mirrors, a non-corner source on one of four edges, a path of at least three cells, and either boundary or less-frequent active-stopper termination.; Reduced the public interface from six mixed semantic/nuisance controls to three exact answer-bearing controls: edge, turn_count, and termination. Canvas dimensions and decoy count remain difficulty-aware nuisance variation rather than advertised axes.; Added strict call validation, a recursive returned-grid self_check, observe_overrides, an independent Python rule mirror, answer-bearing profile extraction, deterministic construction, fresh returns, and a canonical RULE_HASH pin.; Added ten focused regression groups covering all public pairs/profiles, stable prior and diversity, every exact axis value and pairwise boundary, active route branches, D4 mirror-slope transforms, off-route-decoy invariance, destructive mutations, source synchronization, replay determinism, fresh returns, provenance, and global RNG isolation.; Added an independent 30000-draw main/stability census, a reconstruction of the committed version-2 distribution, and a 497-case Racket parity audit spanning public, generated, D4 profile, exact-axis, zero/four-turn, corner/interior-source, active-stopper, and dense-decoy cases.
summary: Find the first red 2 source. Infer its inward direction from the source edge in top, bottom, left, right precedence, with rightward fallback for a non-edge source. Advance one cell at a time for at most 500 steps. Stop before a gray 5 or after leaving the grid; otherwise paint the visited cell cyan 8, turn on slash 7 by (dr,dc)=(-dc,-dr), and turn on backslash 6 by (dr,dc)=(dc,dr). The output is an otherwise-zero grid of the same dimensions.
